name: Light Reaction
pitch: Makes a Bluetooth RGB light glow in the colour of your screen.
hardestProblem: TODO: confirm. Code evidence: working out the light's vendor-specific BLE command protocol by testing (power-off sequence with fallbacks, RGB-restore for power-on).
result: Screen colour sync to the physical light works. No performance metrics recorded. TODO: add if measured.
highlights: Built a screen-reactive 'Ambilight' for a Bluetooth LE RGB light in Python, capturing the display with mss/Pillow and streaming averaged colour over BLE with bleak.
Designed a single-process asyncio backend (aiohttp REST + WebSocket) that coordinates BLE I/O, screen capture and live UI updates on one event loop.
Built a local browser dashboard (vanilla JS) with BLE device scanning, mode switching (sync / manual / off), monitor selection, brightness, presets and live colour preview.
Added adjustable sync rate (3-15 FPS) and a colour-change threshold to limit BLE writes.
Worked out the light's vendor-specific 9-byte command protocol by testing, including a power-off sequence with fallbacks, and wrote a CLI tester and GATT inspection endpoint to support it.
Supports multi-monitor setups by enumerating displays with mss and letting the user choose the capture source.
